already-have.reason: None of the five sub-proposals is implemented and no recorded owner decision contradicts them. (1) MSPLIM: `grep MSPLIM secure/src` is empty; every linker script sets only `_stack_start = ORIGIN(RAM)+LENGTH(RAM)` (secure/memory*.x) with no lower bound; fsbl/src/main.rs:172 and fsbl/src/manifest.rs:30 explicitly say "no MSPLIM"; docs/security/adversarial-review/secure-runtime-resource-adversarial-review.md:45 (RT4) rates the missing MSPLIM/PSPLIM lower bound a HIGH-PRIORITY OPEN SURFACE. (2) ECC/NMI: docs/security/brownout-hardening.md:322 records "ECC double-bit NMI reporting: off (RAMCFG untouched); double-bit = silent corruption"; gh #48 (OPEN, ship-blocker) is exactly this item and is unclosed. (3) Page-123 tag: secure/src/hw/flash.rs:1416-1424 documents the 16-byte QW as `slot_key(8)|type(1)|count(7)` with no MAC/CRC; the only hits for hmac/tag/cmac in offchain_state.rs are prose ("receipt"), and gh #93 (FVX-2) confirms "the 16-byte QW format has no per-entry integrity tag". (4) Page-124: flash.rs:768 "Programmed sentinel: [0x00;16]. Blank sentinel: [0xFF;16]", flash.rs:779 "successful unlock: page blank (all 0xFF)", and `pin_attempts_scan_forward/reverse` (flash.rs:825-895) count non-0xFF QWs, so an erased or stuck-at-0xFF read decodes to 0 attempts; the only mitigation is the F-15.r5 forward+reverse double scan, not an encoding. (5) Kani fault-model for the decoders: gh #397 says the current page-124 Kani model "under-models the security-load-bearing part" and is unstarted. The Trezor-port memory (project_trezor_critical_port_2026_06.md) declines only the secmon port; trezor-comparison.md:634-645 lists "MSPLIM disable at the FSBL→firmware handoff" as a P2 port, which presupposes MSPLIM is set — it is not. CLAUDE.md's only relevant decisions (no new per-signature flash state beyond page-123; SE counters are the PIN authority) are compatible with the proposal as written.
already-have.corrections: Partially tracked — fold into existing issues rather than opening fresh ones: (a) ECC-on SRAM2 + double-error-as-tamper = gh #48 (OPEN, ship-blocker, priority:high); the isolated ECC-NMI model = gh #542 FA-2.2; note gh #150 (F5/TZGW-1): RAMCFG is currently NS-attributed, so routing the ECC NMI to zeroize requires securing RAMCFG first or NS can mask it. Also doc drift: brownout-hardening.md:321 says SRAM ECC is "always active; no config needed", but #48 states SRAM2_ECC is an FLASH_OPTR option bit (bit 24, inverted polarity) — it must be explicitly enabled in the option-byte ceremony. (b) Stack lower-bound/guard policy = gh #542 FA-2.0/2.1 (OPEN-RAM-1 "guard/fault policy") and the ship-blocker gh #374 (worst-case stack bound); MSPLIM programming is the natural implementation of that frozen guard policy but neither issue names MSPLIM — add it to #542 explicitly. (c) Page-123 integrity = gh #93 (FVX-2, asks for a per-entry CRC/commit bit), gh #92 (torn-erase atomicity), gh #230 (crash-atomic compaction); a DHUK-rooted set tag is a strict superset of #93's ask and should be designed together with #230's ping-pong/generation marker, since a tag written as "the last quadword of each commit" interacts with torn-QW replay (#93) and compaction replay order (#230). (d) Page-124 Hamming encoding: no issue exists; only gh #397 (Kani scan/bump monotonicity) touches the decoder. Design caveat the proposal must address: page 124 is legitimately erased (all-0xFF) after every successful unlock (flash.rs:779), so "neither 0x00..00 nor 0xFF..FF is well-formed" only helps if an "initialized" header record is programmed at page-reset time; otherwise an attacker who forces the whole page to read 0xFF still decodes 0 attempts — this is the same guard-key/initialized-state property that makes Trezor's blockwise log work, not the 01/10 expansion alone. (e) Kani fault-model work partially exists as #397; extend it rather than creating a parallel harness. Could not check: whether an owner decision on page-124 layout exists in GitHub issue comments (only titles/bodies were searched) or in closed-issue comment threads.
